inventory.pattern: object pronoun after a preposition (with me / for him)
inventory.gap: wrote 'with I trying to learn'; nouns hide it, only pronouns expose it
inventory.example: With me being the only reviewer, it took a week.

inventory.gap: packs a secondary fact into the main sentence instead of a separate short clause; never used in 45 exchanges
inventory.example: With everyone booking at once, tickets are impossible.

inventory.pattern: purpose nouns (a learning system, not a system for learning)
inventory.gap: reaches for 'a platform where we can...' or a bare noun; never stacks the purpose noun in front. 0 uses in 45 exchanges
inventory.example: Rednote is a great recipe-sharing platform.

cards.cue: 大家都挤在同一时间订票，火车票根本抢不到。
cards.task: Everyone books at the same time. It is impossible to get train tickets.
cards.answer: With everyone booking at the same time, it's impossible to get train tickets.
cards.said: It's impossible to get train tickets with everyone booking at the same time.
cards.why: Structure correct. Position is a separate habit - see What Went Wrong.

cards.cue: 父母家四小时车程，回一趟就把整个周末吃掉了。
cards.task: My parents are four hours away. A trip back eats the whole weekend.
cards.answer: With my parents four hours away, a trip back eats the whole weekend.
cards.said: A trip back eats the whole weekend with my parents four hours away.
cards.why: No participle needed here - an adjective phrase attaches directly. Handled correctly.

cards.cue: 工作和学新东西占掉了大部分时间，现在看小说算是奢侈了。
cards.task: Work and new things take up most of my time. Reading a novel is a luxury these days.
cards.answer: With work and new things taking up most of my time, reading a novel is a luxury these days.
cards.said: Reading a novel is a luxury these days with work and new things taking up most my time.
cards.why: Structure correct. `most my time` -> `most of my time` is not the pattern and was not counted.

cards.cue: 我想学的东西太多，红色警戒一直拖着没玩。
cards.task: I have got so much I am trying to learn. I never get round to Red Alert.
cards.answer: With so much I'm trying to learn, I never get round to Red Alert.
cards.said: I never get round to Red Alert with I trying to learn so much.
cards.why: `with` is a preposition, so a pronoun after it takes the object form - `with me trying`, never `with I trying`. Nouns hide this because they do not inflect, which is why only this item exposed it. Smoother still: `with so much on my plate`.

cards.cue: 短裤卖完了，最后我只买了水果就走了。
cards.task: The shorts were sold out. I ended up leaving with just the fruit.
cards.answer: With the shorts sold out, I ended up leaving with just the fruit.
cards.said: I ended up leaving with just the fruit with the shorts sold out.
cards.why: Form correct. But this item forces the front position: the sentence already contains a real preposition `with just the fruit`, so trailing the pattern puts two unrelated `with`s in one sentence and the listener has to work out which is which.

cards.cue: 大家都在家办公，办公室里冷清得很。
cards.task: Everyone was working from home. The office felt dead.
cards.answer: The office felt dead with everyone working from home.
cards.said: The office felt dead with everyone working from home.
cards.why: Active, so `-ing`. Correct.

cards.cue: 短信服务商正在更换中，所以我得把每个地方都测一遍。
cards.task: The SMS provider is being swapped out right now. I have got to test everything.
cards.answer: With the SMS provider being swapped out right now, I've got to test everything.
cards.said: With the SMS provider being swapped out right now, I've got to test everyting.
cards.why: The hardest item in the drill - passive and still in progress, so `being` is required. Identified unprompted.

cards.cue: 截止时间改到了周三，市场部就不再催我了。
cards.task: The deadline has been moved to Wednesday. Marketing has stopped chasing me.
cards.answer: With the deadline moved to Wednesday, marketing has stopped chasing me.
cards.said: With the deadline moved to Wednesday, marketing has stopped chasing me.
cards.why: Passive but finished, so no `being`. The contrast with item 3 is the whole point of the round, and both were judged correctly.

cards.cue: 大家都挤在同一周抢票，所以我宁愿开车回去也不坐车。
cards.task: Someone asks why you drive home for National Day instead of taking the train. Use the pattern, with "everyone squeezed into the same week" as the background.
cards.answer: With everyone buying train tickets in the same week, I'd rather drive back than take the train.
cards.said: With everyone buying train tickets at the same week, I prefer driving car back rather than taking train.
cards.why: Pattern correct. `at the same week` -> `in the same week` and the missing article in `driving car back` are ordinary chat repairs, not the pattern, and were not counted here.

cards.cue: 因为动到了核心逻辑，我估得得一周左右。
cards.task: You are explaining to a colleague why the ticket needs a week, with "the core logic was touched" as the background.
cards.answer: With the core logic touched, I'd put it closer to a week.
cards.said: With the core logic touched, I'd put it closer to a week.
cards.why: Passive and finished, so no `being` - correct. `I'd put it closer to a week` is `C024`, produced with no prompting.

cards.cue: 把东西都关了之后，我下班后能专心看书。
cards.task: Describe your state after work once the phone or the devices are off.
cards.answer: With everything shut off, I can focus on reading after work.
cards.said: With everything shut off, I can focus on reading books after work.
cards.why: Correct. Chose the participle route over the simpler `with my phone off`, which is the harder of the two.

cards.cue: 一个分享菜谱的平台
cards.task: 一个分享菜谱的平台
cards.answer: a recipe-sharing platform
cards.said: a recipe-sharing platform

cards.cue: 一个游戏论坛
cards.task: 一个游戏论坛
cards.answer: a gaming forum
cards.said: a gaming forum
cards.why: Day 07 produced `a game forum`, which passes; `gaming` is the idiomatic choice.

cards.cue: 一个发短信的服务
cards.task: 一个发短信的服务
cards.answer: an SMS-sending service
cards.said: a SMS-sending service
cards.why: The stack is right; the article is not. `a` vs `an` follows pronunciation, not spelling - `SMS` opens on /e/, so it takes `an`. Same class: `an FBI agent`, `an hour`, `an MBA`; and inversely `a university`, `a European`, both opening on /j/.

cards.cue: 一个监控接口的看板
cards.task: 一个监控接口的看板
cards.answer: an API monitoring dashboard
cards.said: a monitoring dashboard
cards.why: Already produced in Day 05 as a three-noun stack, unprompted, before this pattern was ever named.

cards.cue: 一本讲投资的书
cards.task: 一本讲投资的书
cards.answer: a book about investing
cards.said: a book about investing
cards.why: Content, so no stacking. Trap correctly refused.

cards.cue: 一个学投资的 App
cards.task: 一个学投资的 App
cards.answer: an investing app
cards.said: an APP about learning investing
cards.why: The one stackable item hidden among the traps. An app is built to do a job, not to discuss a topic - it is *for* investing, not *about* investing. Two side notes: `APP` in capitals is a Chinese-internet convention, English writes `app`; and `learning investing` collides two `-ing`s, which is why native usage drops one. `an app for learning to invest` is also entirely correct, just uncompressed.

cards.cue: 一场关于业务逻辑的讨论
cards.task: 一场关于业务逻辑的讨论
cards.answer: a discussion about business logic
cards.said: a discussion about business logic
cards.why: Content again. Correctly refused.

cards.cue: 一个测试短信服务的脚本
cards.task: 一个测试短信服务的脚本
cards.answer: an SMS service test script
cards.said: an SMS service test script
cards.why: Four nouns in a row, and the article corrected from item 1.3 without being told.

cards.cue: 一个讲远程办公的播客
cards.task: 一个讲远程办公的播客
cards.answer: a podcast about remote work
cards.said: a podcast about remote job
cards.why: Correctly refused to stack. Not counted against the pattern: `remote job` -> `remote work` - a `job` is the position you hold, `work` is the activity, and a podcast is about the latter.

cards.cue: 有人问你小红书是什么，你介绍一下。
cards.task: Someone asks what Rednote is. Introduce it.
cards.answer: Rednote is a life-sharing platform.
cards.said: Rednote is a life-sharing platform.
cards.why: Built a compound that was never taught, and it is idiomatic.

cards.cue: 跟同事说你们有个东西能监控服务挂没挂。
cards.task: Tell a colleague you have something that monitors whether a service is down.
cards.answer: We've got a monitoring dashboard to check whether the service is down.
cards.said: We've got a monitoring dashboard to check whether the service is down.

cards.cue: 解释你周末学投资都用什么。
cards.task: Explain what you use to learn about investing at weekends.
cards.answer: Xueqiu is an investing app that helps me keep an eye on what's happening across different industries.
cards.said: Xueqiu is an investing app which helps me keep an eye on development trends from different industries.
cards.why: Pattern correct, and it is the exact phrase missed in 2.2, self-corrected with no prompting. Not counted against the pattern: `which` -> `that` in a defining clause is the more common spoken choice, and `development trends from different industries` is a shade written for speech.
